subject: Mechanical Engineering
title: The Double Crank: Both Sides Spin
description: A 60-second lesson on The Double Crank: Both Sides Spin.

hook.text: In some four-bar linkages, both grounded links can spin fully.

buildup.text: When the shortest link is the fixed frame, both side links become cranks.

discovery.text: The two cranks spin at varying speed ratios through each revolution.

twist.text: The coupler link wobbles wildly, tracing complex curves in space.

climax.text: Locomotive drive wheels once used double cranks to link drivers together.

punchline.text: Fix the shortest link and both neighbors spin free.

quiz.question: When does a four-bar linkage become a double crank?
options: When the longest link is fixed to the frame
When the shortest link is fixed so both adjacent links rotate fully
When all four links are the same length
